notes:
Summary: procurement-stage SLA negotiation for Dedicated GPU pool to support fleet chat + reranking workloads. Customer requires hard throughput guarantees (sustained 4k tokens/sec across 8 concurrent models) and tight p95 latency (<= 150ms gen for short prompts).

Key requirements / asks:
- Throughput: reserved capacity plan for 1200 simultaneous low-latency sessions (estimate) + burst pool for seasonal peaks. Wants explicit GPU reservation counts and fallback model mapping.
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 targets requested. They insist p95 <= 150ms for 8k-token avg session (short chats) for the primary model family.
- Uptime & credits: legal demands uptime >= 99.95% for Dedicated; proposed credit schedule: 99.9-99.95 => 10% credit, 99.5-99.9 => 25% credit, <99.5 => 50% credit. They counter-request cap at 30% for aggregate year.
- Maintenance windows: they want maintenance limited to Sunday 02:00-06:00 PST and maximum cumulative maintenance 6 hours/month. Redwood initial proposal allowed 12 hours/month with 72-hour advance notice.
- Support SLAs: P1 response 15m / P1 remediation target 4 hours, P2 response 1hr, P3 response 4hr. They asked for 24/7 on-call escalation for P1.
- Data & security: SOC2 + ISO27001 proof, KMS/HSM integration for private deployment, audit log retention 3 years, EU data residency for EU fleets.
- Termination/performance: want right-to-terminate for repeated SLA breaches (>=2 incidents in a 6mo rolling window) and prorated refunds.

Recent timeline (bulleted quick log):
- 2026-01-20: Intro call (Jordan) — overview of workloads, initial sizing exercise. customer: "latency is the business metric".
- 2026-01-27: Technical deep-dive with SE (Priya) — model mix (open LLM fine-tuned + small reranker), KV cache expectations, quantization tolerance noted.
- 2026-02-14: POC kickoff (ff_20260214_9b3d) — 2-week POC running on dedicated pilot cluster (4xA100 equiv). Focus: steady-state throughput and prefix cache behavior.
- 2026-02-24: POC interim review — observed p95 ~190ms for some flows under load; SE proposing kernel/compilation tweaks and additional GPU headroom.
- 2026-03-02: Legal + procurement sync (ff_20260302_1a8f) — discussed credit schedules, maintenance windows, liability caps. Customer pushed for stronger credits and narrower maintenance.
- 2026-03-08: Exec recap (Jordan/Priya) — estimated committed ARR asked, procurement asked for formal proposal to review with CFO.

Technical notes / tradeoffs observed:
- Prefetch & KV caching reduces per-token cost by ~18% in POC, but cold-start p95 spikes remain for rare routes. Need prefix caching and warmed instances for SLAs.
- Quantization to 4-bit looks acceptable for reranking; primary chat model best with fp16 for quality. Customer open to guided quant profiles to hit latency targets.
- Routing policy: customer requires deterministic fallback to smaller model rather than outright failure when burst capacity engaged. Needs SLA on fallback behavior.

Open/legal negotiating points (action items):
- Finalize credit schedule cap (legal currently holding at max 30% aggregate credits/yr).
- Maintenance window dispute: propose compromise: 8 hours/month, 90-day notice for major upgrades, emergency maintenance defined with <2hr notice and additional credits.
- Support: add named on-call contact and P1 escalation matrix to SOW.
- KMS: plan for staged on-prem KMS POC; require sample integration runbook.

Next steps (short):
- Jordan to send revised SOW and updated credit schedule proposal (due 2026-03-12).
- Priya to run extended POC with warmed persistent instances and kernel tuning; deliver p95 report by 2026-03-18.
- Legal: coordinate Redwood legal + Noble Arc procurement week of 2026-03-15.
